qs.q: What is the primary underlying immunopathogenic mechanism of IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein Purpura)?
qs.e: IgA vasculitis is classified as a small vessel vasculitis caused by a type III hypersensitivity reaction associated with IgA deposition. It is not mediated by IgE or direct cytotoxic T-cells.

qs.q: Concerning Henoch-schonlein purpura, which of the following statements is true?
o: Most children do not recover and die within a few days of diagnosis
The condition predominantly affects large vessels located in the body
The underlying pathophysiology is primarily mediated by IgG antibodies
The condition is a small vessel vasculitis that is IgA mediated
qs.e: Henoch-schonlein purpura is recognized as a small-vessel vasculitis that is mediated by IgA immune complexes. It is generally a self-limiting condition in children rather than a rapidly fatal illness.
